title: Be an Astronaut
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for Shellfie.

pages: Today, you are an astronaut! You live and work on a space station that flies around the Earth.
Inside the station you wear comfy clothes. To go outside for a spacewalk, you wear a big white spacesuit with its own air.
In space, everything floats. You let go of your toothbrush for one second, and it floats away. You chase it across the room.
Lunch comes in pouches. You squeeze out a blob of juice, and it floats in the air like a wobbly ball. You catch it with your mouth. Gulp!
Your job is to do science experiments, fix things on the station, and take care of your body. You exercise for about two hours every day so your muscles stay strong.
At night, you sleep in a sleeping bag tied to the wall, so you do not float around and bump into your friends.
You work with a crew from different countries, and with a team on the ground called Mission Control. They talk to you on the radio every day.
The best part? Looking out the window at the Earth. The station goes around so fast that you can see about 16 sunrises every day!
The hardest part? You are far from your family for months, and you can not go outside to play.

How do you become an astronaut? Go to college to study science, math, or engineering. Then study more, and work for a few years. Astronaut training takes about 2 more years. It can take more than 10 years in all!
What can you do now? Look at the moon and the stars. Visit a science museum or a planetarium. Build a model rocket with a grown-up.
